title: Rates of trait evolution that vary among branches
text: Ecological hypotheses rates often history lineages: evolution faster one habitat another, burst colonising new region, slowdown lineages accumulate region. trait_mk() simulates history discrete character along tree, history_rates() turns rate branch, mean branch rate depends history moment. "state", habitat rate, Brownian motion several regimes (O’Meara et al. 2006). "burst", change habitat multiplies rate, excess decays time, along descending branches , following expectation selection strongest lineage first adapts new community (McPeek 2017). title: Getting started with comdynamite

what: Traits under one or several adaptive optima
title: Getting started with comdynamite
text: trait_ou() simulates traits Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process (Hansen 1997). alpha = 0 Brownian motion; alpha > 0 traits pulled towards optimum, paint_regimes() gives clades optimum (multi-peak OU; Butler & King 2004).
code: pool <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(32) node <- ape::getMRCA(pool, pool$tip.label[1:8]) in_clade <- rownames(trait_ou(pool)) %in% ape::extract.clade(pool, node)$tip.label reg <- paint_regimes(pool, nodes = node) x_ou <- trait_ou(pool, alpha = 2, theta = c(`0` = 0, `1` = 5), regimes = reg) tapply(x_ou[, 1], ifelse(in_clade, "clade (optimum 5)", "rest (optimum 0)"), mean) #> clade (optimum 5)  rest (optimum 0)  #>         3.8228309         0.1872388

title: Getting started with comdynamite
text: Besides population dynamics, comdynamite can assemble local community regional pool fixed rules, Kraft et al. (2007). Species removed one time community reaches chosen size: "limiting_similarity": GAUSE algorithm Colwell & Winkler (1984), Kraft et al. (2007) used competition. pair species closest trait space, one smaller sum distances remaining species removed, . "filtering": species farthest niche optimum (ancestral state derived corner trait space) removed first. "neutral": species drawn random. many pools, mean phylogenetic distance (MPD) among community members shows expected contrast traits evolve Brownian motion: average, limiting similarity keeps distant relatives neutral assembly (higher MPD), filtering keeps closer relatives (lower MPD), although single replicates vary.
code: pool <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(32) x <- trait_ou(pool, n_traits = 2) assemble_community(x, size = 16, rule = "limiting_similarity")$community #>  [1] "t1"  "t3"  "t6"  "t9"  "t10" "t13" "t14" "t17" "t19" "t22" "t26" "t27" #> [13] "t29" "t30" "t31" "t32" mpd <- function(tree, sp) mean(as.dist(ape::cophenetic.phylo(tree)[sp, sp])) rules <- c("limiting_similarity", "filtering", "neutral") res <- replicate(100, {   pool <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(32)   x <- trait_ou(pool, n_traits = 2)   sapply(rules, function(r) mpd(pool, assemble_community(x, 16, r)$community)) }) rowMeans(res) #> limiting_similarity           filtering             neutral  #>            1.551878            1.444317            1.502199

what: Step 2: write the method as a function
title: Evaluating a method with simulated metacommunities
text: method evaluation proportion variation Hellinger- transformed abundances (Legendre & Gallagher 2001) explained one predictor, redundancy analysis, permutation test.
code: r2_env <- function(y, x) {   y <- scale(y, scale = FALSE)   x <- x - mean(x)   sum((crossprod(x, y) / sum(x^2))^2) * sum(x^2) / sum(y^2) } p_value <- function(y, x, perms) {   obs <- r2_env(y, x)   null <- apply(perms, 1, function(p) r2_env(y, x[p]))   (sum(null >= obs) + 1) / (length(null) + 1) }

code: n_perm <- 199 free <- t(replicate(n_perm, sample(side^2))) torus <- torus_permutations(side) restricted <- torus[sample(nrow(torus), n_perm), ]  y <- vegan::decostand(sim$abundance[, colSums(sim$abundance) > 0], "hellinger") p_value(y, unrelated, free) p_value(y, unrelated, restricted)

code: results <- readRDS("evaluating-methods.rds") rates <- aggregate(p ~ predictor + null_model + lambda, data = results,                    FUN = function(p) mean(p <= 0.05)) names(rates)[names(rates) == "p"] <- "rejection_rate" rates$se <- sqrt(rates$rejection_rate * (1 - rates$rejection_rate) / 200) knitr::kable(rates, digits = 3) h <- results[results$predictor == "unrelated", ] old <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1), mgp = c(2.4, 0.7, 0)) for (n in c("free", "torus")) {   hist(h$p[h$null_model == n], breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.05), col = "#0072B2",        border = "white", main = paste(n, "permutations"), xlab = "p-value") } par(old)

title: Known biogeographic histories for Herodotools
text: areas evolve along tree discrete trait, trait_mk(), whose states regions. result keeps every change, simmap format phytools. species can occur sites region, region_pool() pool argument simulate_metacommunity(). 20 sites split two regions. as_herodotools() names parts arguments Herodotools, ancestral.area holds true area node. true ages lineage arrived region site come history: Herodotools dates arrival age oldest ancestor node region, can see arrivals nodes.
